en: "Whoaaa, the Prince just fell out of the sky!?"{w}
Goblin Below
note: Literally 'voice of the goblin below'; shortened for the name box. The matching ogre name box (slice 048, [JP]) should read 'Ogre Below'.

en: "Prince!?{w}PRIIIIINCE!!"{w}
"I-I really thought... I was going to die, you know...?"{w}
note: Montana slips into dazed polite speech ([JP]); kept as a stunned, shaky line.

en: "Young Lord, a dive with no rope at all -- who could have imagined?{w}I am utterly in awe."{w}
note: [JP] (the retainer's address for Montana) = 'Young Lord' throughout this slice. [JP] = a 'bare' dive, i.e. the rope was never tied.

en: "Man, you're amazing!{w}You actually pulled off a bungee jump without a lifeline!{w}I've got no choice but to give you credit for this!!"{w}{p}"If you're up for it, show us again sometime!!"{w}
"I am never... doing that again..."{w}
"Now then, Young Lord. As for what comes after the bungee jump..."{w}
"Whaaat!?{w}There's still something else I have to do!?"{w}
"There is no need to brace yourself so.{w}You need only go and report to the royal tomb in the Churos Highlands."{w}
"Aww, is that all?{w}Then let's knock it out real quick."{w}
"I would like that as well, but I am busy, as is everyone else, so none of us are able to accompany you..."{w}
note: [JP] read as agreeing to 'finish it quickly' (the previous line); the 'but' sets up the refusal to go along.

en: "...You don't need an escort or anything, do you?"{w}
"Excuse me!?"{w}
"Well, as I said.{w}Please go on your own, Young Lord.{w}As in, get going already."{w}
note: [JP] drops the retainer's politeness into blunt casual speech; 'get going already' keeps the rude turn.

en: "Um, look, I'm... the king, right?"{w}
"Of course."{w}
"It'd be a problem if I died, right?"{w}
"Moderately."{w}
"In the event of your royal demise, we would have to choose the next king from among the ogres, wouldn't we?{w}A mere half day. What a short reign it was..."{w}
note: [JP] is the formal word for a monarch's death; 'royal demise' keeps the mock solemnity.

en: "Wait just a minuuute!!"{w}
"Oh, honestly. Don't make that face.{w}Pardon me, adventurers.{w}This is such a bother, so please just humor him for me."{w}
note: [JP] read as the retainer's own bother ('it's a hassle'), which is what provokes Montana's next line.

en: "What kind of way to ask is that!? Fine, forget it!{w}Hey, you all. That's how things are, so... won't you come to Churos with me?"{w}{p}"Oh, come to think of it, I never told you my name, did I?{w}It's Montana. Nice to meet ya!"{w}
Montana
"Huh? I was gonna come with you, but someone already beat me to it!{w}Jeez, come on, seriously."{w}
note: Shown when the party has no free slot: [JP] = 'someone got there first'. Kept literal rather than naming the party limit.

en: Goblin Prince joined the party.{w}
"Do have a safe trip."{w}
"...Grr. That ticks me off."{w}
note: [JP] is a childish form of [JP]; rendered as a sulky grumble.

en: "Come now, come now. Off to the Churos Highlands with the Young Lord, if you please."{w}
"Oh, are you ready?"{w}
"Alrighty!"{w}
"Oh, it's you.{w}There isn't much here, but make yourselves at home."{w}
"Oh, it's you.{w}There isn't much here, but make yourselves at... Huh?{w}The Yuan Wine?"{w}
note: Same opening as 2789, interrupted at the same point ([JP]...).

en: "What!? Good adventurers, where did you hear of that!?{w}...From Princess Leafa of Isfald!?{w}Oh, at last... at laaast!!"{w}
note: The party carries Leafa's royal command, not the wine itself (Montana fetches it in 2803-2807), so [JP] = the matter of the wine: 'hear of that'. The middle line answers an unshown reply from the party.

en: "Wh-what is it, what is it? What's gotten into you?"{w}
"Young Lord, this is the important duty your predecessor told you of at the Churos Highlands!"{w}
note: [JP] = the previous ruler; 'your predecessor' avoids guessing kinship or gender. 'At the Churos Highlands' attached to 'told' as in the source (the royal tomb is there).

en: "...No way.{w}Wasn't that just a legend handed down for generations?{w}And it's in MY generation... that we hit the jackpot?"{w}
"So it would seem!{w}Now then, Young Lord! I shall show you the way, so please carry it in your own hands!"{w}
"This is turning into something pretty huge...{w}Hang on a sec, okay?"{w}
"So this is it...{w}The Yuan Wine. It's ridiculously old."{w}

"The elven royal family sends out the call, we ogres and goblins answer it, and we hand over this wine."{w}{p}"From an age so ancient it feels wrong to simply call it 'long ago'... a promise that has carried on ever since.{w}I'll fulfill it now. Please, accept it."{w}
note: Montana switches from [JP] to [JP] here; the more solemn register is kept for this one speech.

en:
[Key Item]
You obtained the Yuan Wine.{w}
"Ngh... nnnghhh..."{w}
note: The retainer choking back tears (explained in 2814).

en: "What's up with you?"{w}
"To think I would witness a fragment of such a legend with my own eyes while I still live.{w}...And on top of that, you even look just a little dignified, Young Lord."{w}
"Oh, come on..."{w}{p}"Anyway, I guess this'll do?{w}I'll leave the rest to Princess Leafa and you all.{w}I'm counting on you, okay?"{w}
"What's this, who're you lot? Don't get visitors like you often."{w}

"What, you want grapes?{w}Can't just hand those over that easily...{w}I know, do me a favor."{w}{p}"My loincloth's on 1F. Take it to Hostef, over in the northwest, to get it washed.{w}Do that, and I'll give you some grapes."{w}
note: [JP] here and Hostef's [JP] (2935, 2941) both rendered 'loincloth' so the player connects them.

en: "If you don't take my loincloth in for washing, you're not getting any grapes, got it?"{w}
"Oh, you took it in for washing for me!{w}Then go ahead and take the grapes.{w}Thanks a bunch."{w}
"Welp, guess I'll go hunt for the bungee gear.{w}Knowing that cowardly Prince, he probably went and dumped it on the sly."{w}
"The Prince is something else...{w}I seriously respect the guy..."{w}
note: Said to the party after the jump (Montana is not addressed), so third person.

en: Ogre Caretaker
"Whaddaya want, you folks?{w}I'm tellin' ya for your own good -- best head on home, quick."{w}
note: Caretaker speaks rural dialect ([JP], [JP], [JP]); rendered as light rustic English.

en: "Huh? Ya want grapes?{w}I'm just the caretaker, so that ain't for me to decide...{w}Best go ask the Ogre Knight, respectful-like."{w}
note: [JP]: the Ogre Knight's gender is not established, so no Sir/Master; the deference goes into 'respectful-like' ([JP]).

en: "Ya got the say-so for the grapes?{w}Well, ain't that good.{w}Right, I'll pick ya some, so wait there."{w}

[Key Item]
You obtained Ogre Grapes.{w}
note: New item name: Ogre Grapes ([JP]), not in the glossary.

en: "Here, take 'em with ya."{w}{p}"...What, ya ain't gonna eat 'em yourselves?{w}Aw, so they're for the alchemy doc, eh.{w}Then a smaller bunch woulda done fine."{w}{p}"Come back 'round when the harvest's done.{w}Ya got permission, so I'll share a little with you folks too."{w}
note: [JP] = the Alchemy Geezer (who asks for the grapes, slice 050); 'the alchemy doc' keeps [JP]'s respect in the caretaker's voice.

en: "Why's that, I wonder...{w}Us ogres, we been growin' grapes forever."{w}{p}"They say no matter how handy the goblins are, this one job ya must never leave to 'em."{w}{p}"I don't understand hard stuff like that, but...{w}sometimes, when I'm lookin' at the grapes, I get this warm, achin' sorta feelin'."{w}{p}"Why's that, I wonder..."{w}
note: [JP] read as 'however dexterous the goblins are' (goblins are the skilled-handed ones in this fort).

en: Hostef
"Well, what is it now? You've come to see Hostef, then?{w}Do not get in the way of my laundry, thank you kindly."{w}
note: Hostef speaks in tanka rhythm (5-7-5 / 7-7) in every line; English keeps a 5-7-5 / 7-7 syllable cadence where possible. Third-person self-reference ([JP]) kept.

en: "You again, is it? Is it a tanka you want, by any chance, hm?{w}I'd gladly give you one, but I need some material."{w}
"Come to think of it, the Ogre Knight's loincloth, that's one{w}I have yet to wash. Whatever shall I do now?"{w}

"Oh, thank you so much! You brought the loincloth to me, came all the way here.{w}As thanks, I'll present to you a tanka of my own make."{w}{p}".........."{w}{p}'So long overdue,
I do the wash -- and up on
the rooftop there gleams{w}a loincloth in the sunlight,
here at Baroque Fort.'{w}{p}"Here you are, take it. I present it to you now. Take good care of it.{w}And with that said, I will go back to my work once again."{w}
note: The tanka parodies a classical poem: [JP] is a pillow word for light/sun, so 'sunlight' carries it alongside [JP]. Laid out on lines as a poem; {w} stays after the third line as in the source. Last line has 5 syllables, not 7.

en:
[Key Item]
You obtained Hostef's Tanka.{w}
"Hello, hello there! Perfect weather for laundry, such a lovely day.{w}After this, why don't we have some tea together, perhaps?"{w}
"Whoa there!? Who's that, barging in all of a sudden!{w}You gave me quite a fright.{w}What brings you here? Adventuring all the way out to a place like this?"{w}
Pyroglyph Researcher
note: Glossary form; 20 characters, over the ~16 name-box guide. Check fit in game.

en:
"I study an ancient script called Pyroglyph.{w}This is what the ancient script looks like."{w}{p}
              '  ┴├┣┣┫  '{w}{p}"Surprised?{w}It means 'hello'."{w}{p}"There seem to be plenty of other words too.{w}Unfortunately, I don't have enough material, so I haven't been able to decipher all of it."{w}{p}"When I was young, I went out and gathered material on my own two feet, but I'm getting on in years now..."{w}
note: Box-drawing glyphs kept verbatim: they are the Pyroglyph cipher. By the letter tables in 2959-2963 they spell H-E-L-L-O, so 'hello' works in English as is. Full-width centring spaces converted to ASCII spaces (trailing ones dropped).

en: "You folks are going to keep on adventuring from here on, aren't you?{w}Then how about doing me a favor?"{w}{p}"Oh, it's nothing much.{w}If you come across any Pyroglyph, I'd like you to let me know and help with my research."{w}
Help with the research?

"Is that so? You'll do it!{w}That's a great help, thank you!"{w}{p}"Pyroglyph can be seen in places like the Dekor Temple Ruins, so would you remember what it says and where you found it?"{w}{p}"When you come back, let's work on deciphering it together.{w}I'm counting on you, truly."{w}
"I see...{w}Well, can't be helped. I'll try someone else."{w}

"Oh, good of you to come.{w}I've kept up my research since then, and I've figured out a few things."{w}{p}"Pyroglyph resembles the letters we use, you see -- each symbol matches up with one letter."{w}{p}"For example, what I know right now is that{w}FJPQSUVXYZ{w}match up with ┬┓┻┠┨┿┝┥┸╂, and so on."{w}{p}"So, I want to match up all 26 letters.{w}You'll help me, won't you?"{w}
note: Cipher glyphs kept verbatim; full-width letters converted to ASCII in the same order. [JP] = the Latin alphabet (26 letters), so no change needed for English.

en:
"Now then, first of all...
would you tell me ABCDEFG?"{w}

note: Cipher answer (glyphs for A-G), read by the puzzle; left verbatim.

en:
"Next up...
would you tell me HIJKLMN?"{w}

note: Cipher answer (glyphs for H-N), read by the puzzle; left verbatim.

en:
"Next up...
would you tell me OPQRSTU?"{w}
